chapter: Chicago, Detroit and Seattle Harmony Kings
title: Learning the arrangements and the Seattle Harmony Kings' reputation
summary: Hooven helps him learn an all-arranged book; the band, a Victor recording act, is a class above Chubb-Steinberg and features his mellophone.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: In Detroit. Oh, boy, then my practice started. It was an all arrangement band -- and everyday in my hotel room, I was learning those arrange- ments---
And, Hooven helped you with them---
Oh, sure - we were very close together. He was a great saver in my life with his help.
And, I was still playing just as much
Now, mention this Seattle Harmony Kings--- what they were - now, they were a pretty famous band--- in those days - weren't they?
They actually were from Seattle-- but they hardly ever went back there to play--

Oh, no - at this time, they were on the road and they were playing all the big cities in the Midwest. You know, Detroit, Cleveland, Cincinnati - around in that territory--- and, some in New York, I think; they played there too. But, you know, they had made Victor records and, you know, records were a big thing then too. So, they had a big name and, of course, you know, I wanted to be with that band. And, so, they came and do you know that he kept us there about 16 weeks with that band. It just was an amazing band; of course, it was wonderful for me because I got a chance to really get down to business in my playing.
This was a step above Chubb Stein- berg, I gather---

Oh, Lord yes -- it was really a class band--- you know. And, the fact that he liked--- Eddie liked my mellophone and he used to feature me on the mellophone; they'd make an arrangement and build it around my mellophone.
